title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll dealt The White Wall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The White Wall
options.lineage: white-cube gallery hangs and museum wall labels
options.thesis: Your case studies and your paintings hang on the same white wall, each with a small wall label. Engineer and artist, one exhibition.
options.viewport: Almost empty white wall. One live piece hangs at the centre: a generative lilac drawing your pointer paints into. Next to it sits a wall label: Maya Stuttard, product designer & creative engineer; 'Untitled (you), 2026. Code and your cursor.' One link: Walk the wall.
options.risk: If the labels get chatty or the wall gets crowded, it turns back into the cluttered page you just rejected.

raised.raise: One-voice type: a single type family; hierarchy comes only from size, weight and case.
No-grey commitment: text is ink or lilac, never a mid-grey tint.
The hero piece answers the visitor: calm when idle, it blooms under the pointer and settles when you leave.
Case study pages walk in order, with a clear 'next exhibit' at the end of each one.
Each exhibit gets its own flat lilac-tint mount, so work reads as objects, not cards.

options.label: Wet Wash
options.thesis: The whole site is a sheet of white paper. Your cursor drops lilac watercolour that blooms and dries, and the work sits in the washes.
options.viewport: White paper, your name at scale. Pointer movement bleeds lilac pigment through a fluid simulation; the first case study peeks up from below.
options.risk: The most familiar route for an artist-designer portfolio, and the paint can upstage the work.

options.label: Glaze Shelf
options.lineage: ceramic glaze test tiles on a kiln shelf
options.thesis: Each project is a glazed test piece on a chalk-white shelf, with a recipe card: role, method, participants, result.
options.viewport: One shelf row of lilac glaze pieces; hovering one lets its glaze run toward the recipe card beneath it.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for clarity (recipe card = case metadata), but design leads don't recognise themselves in a kiln.
options.risk: Reads as a craft-pottery site if the recipe cards aren't disciplined.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The portfolio as a live terminal transcript.
options.case: Breaks your white-and-lilac brief and reads developer, not designer.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Barcode fields and sine lattices in pure black and white.
options.case: Cold and dense; the opposite of 'pull someone in'.

options.label: Living Skin
options.thesis: A surface that changes pattern with context.
options.viewport: A pale skin rippling with signals.
options.case: Striking but says nothing about product design.
options.kept: The hero answers the visitor's state.

options.label: Shareware Wizard
options.thesis: The portfolio as a Next > Next > Finish sequence.
options.case: Gimmick; hides the work behind clicks.

options.label: Toy Catalogue
options.thesis: Work packed edge to edge on flat primary sweeps.
options.case: The clutter you asked to remove.
options.kept: Every piece on its own flat colour mount.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean designer portfolio: big intro line, project grid, about, contact, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and one-line intro, then a 2-column grid of case studies.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other portfolio a hiring manager opens that day.
